newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETES LAUNCH BID TO HOST BRITISH ACADEMY OF SPORT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETES LAUNCH BID TO HOST BRITISH ACADEMY OF SPORT.

text.p: A consortium of British athletes and businessmen launched a bid to host a new academy for British sport on Wednesday.

The British Academy of Sport, proposed by Prime Minister John Major in July, is an initiative to boost the performance of Britain's elite athletes after the nation's poor showing at the Atlanta Olympics.
Rowers Steve Redgrave and Matthew Pinsent won Britain's only gold in Atlanta, in the coxless pairs.

The academy proposed by Athletes' Bid, supported by more than 200 world-class British athletes past and present including former Olympic middle distance champion Seb Coe and gold medal decathlete Daley Thompson, would provide training and support facilities for most sports, consortium architect Terry Pawson said.
"This academy will produce more Olympic gold medals for Britain without a shadow of a doubt." said judo's Ray Stevens, who took silver at the Barceolona Olympics.

Many European countries already have central sports academies. Stevens, who was forced to go to Paris to train for the Atlanta Games because of a shortage of sparring partners and facilities in Britain, said a British academy was essential.
"Without the facilities that a central academy, like France's Incep, offers, you're down before you start. You know you can't compete on level terms abroad." Stevens said.

The Athletes' Bid complex would occupy a site on the outskirts of London and could be up and running before the Sydney Olympics, former member of Parliament and bid steering group member Sir Gerard Neil said.
"The Athletes' Bid will give us a pool of information from which to select our future star athletes. That's the key." Roger Utley, former British Lions and England rugby coach, said.

The Athletes' Bid, one of 25 competing for the academy, would, if successful, qualify for 100 million pounds ($164.5 million) funding from the National Lottery set aside by Major. The competing bids are due to be wittled down to six within the next two weeks.
